sentence: This project studies how respiratory neurons are disrupted in rats with hypertension and tests whether improving breathing also improves blood pressure.
This project builds models that predict which young infants with bronchiolitis have low risk of developing respiratory progression.
This project studies why some malaria control practices work less well against mosquitoes and tests whether a malaria vaccine and bed nets reduce disease.
This project studies membrane fusion, the step that releases neurotransmitters, to understand synaptic transmission.
This project builds genetically encoded voltage indicators that let scientists watch electrical activity in living tissues using two-photon microscopes.
This project studies how small extracellular vesicles affect chronic pain after spinal cord injury.
This project studies how spatial and social factors affect the risk and outcomes of invasive fungal infections.
This project uses genomics and bioinformatics analyses to study the role of a network in genome maintenance and cancer.
This project builds lipid nanoparticles that silence long noncoding RNAs linked to metastasis and drug resistance in triple-negative breast cancer.
This project builds a reverse genetic system to manipulate small phages and studies how they compete with much larger viruses.
This project tests whether clonal somatic mutations in microglia drive neuroinflammation and neuronal loss in Alzheimer’s disease.
This project builds a peer-led intervention to improve colorectal cancer screening among adults in public housing and tests it in a randomized controlled trial.
This project builds imaging tools using tissue clearing and two photon microscopy to map inflammation in animal models of tendon injury.
This project studies what makes the bacterial cell envelope strong and how bacteria change it to resist antibiotics.
This project uses deep learning on brain MRI, histopathology and clinico-genomic data to predict how well checkpoint inhibitors work for brain metastases.
This project studies how to target the metabolic dependencies of acute myelogenous leukemia in children and tests a well-tolerated drug.
This project studies how thyroid hormone controls herpes virus infection in neuronal cells.
This project studies how the nervous system maintains the surface of the eye and how this changes under inflammatory and pain conditions.
This project studies how horizontal gene transfer spreads antibiotic resistance on conjugative plasmids, focusing on fitness costs and transfer rates.
This project studies how oxytocin signaling in the dentate gyrus affects how the brain processes social memory.
